name: Starting Strength
author: Mark Rippetoe
structure: Two full-body sessions, alternated. Squat 3x5 every session; bench press and overhead press take turns at 3x5; deadlift 1x5, later taking turns with power cleans 5x3.
progression: Load goes up every session the sets were completed: large steps on squat and deadlift in the first weeks, then about 2.5 kg (5 lb); upper-body lifts 2.5 kg and then less. After a stall, take about 10 % off and build back up.
adapt: The app trains one fixed week, so the A/B alternation becomes A-B-A every week and session B is trained once. The larger early steps are not automatic: set `inc` for the start and lower it at a review.
caveats: Little upper-body and back work, and not written for powerlifting. The size of the reset is common practice and was not checked against the book.

name: StrongLifts 5x5
author: Mehdi Hadim
structure: Two full-body sessions, alternated. A: squat, bench press and barbell row, 5x5 each. B: squat and overhead press 5x5, deadlift 1x5.
progression: All five sets of five done: add 2.5 kg (5 lb) next session. A miss repeats the weight; three sessions missed at the same weight take 10 % off that lift only.
adapt: The app trains one fixed week, so the A/B alternation becomes A-B-A every week and session B is trained once.
caveats: Starts everyone from the empty bar, and squats three times a week against one set of deadlifts.

name: Greyskull LP
author: John Sheaffer; the Phrak variant comes from r/Fitness
structure: Main lifts for two sets of five and a third set of five or more, taken as far as it goes. Bench press and overhead press alternate, squat most sessions, deadlift for the one open set only. The Phrak variant adds chin-ups and rows to every session.
progression: Each session: upper-body lifts up 1.25 kg (2.5 lb), lower-body lifts 2.5 kg (5 lb). A last set far past the target doubles the step. A last set under five reps takes 10 % off that lift.
adapt: The app trains one fixed week, so alternating lifts settle into a fixed A-B-A. The app doubles the step when the last set reaches twice the target.
caveats: More work for size than Starting Strength. The usual mistake is piling accessories on top of it.

name: r/Fitness Basic Beginner Routine
author: the r/Fitness community
structure: Two full-body sessions, alternated. A: barbell row, bench press, squat. B: chin-up, overhead press, deadlift. Each for three sets of five, the last set open-ended.
progression: Each session: upper-body lifts up 1.25 kg (2.5 lb), lower-body lifts 2.5 kg (5 lb); more than ten reps on the last set doubles the step. Fewer than 15 reps across the three sets takes 10 % off. The open set stops one or two reps short of failure.
adapt: The app trains one fixed week, so the A/B alternation becomes A-B-A every week.
caveats: Meant as a bridge of about three months, after which its own wiki sends people on to GZCLP or 5/3/1 for Beginners.

name: GZCLP
author: Cody Lefever
structure: Three tiers a session: a main lift for 5 sets of 3 with the last set open (T1), a second lift for 3x10 (T2), an accessory for 3x15 with the last set open (T3). Four sessions rotate the main lifts: squat, overhead press, bench press, deadlift.
progression: Each session: bench and overhead press up 2.5 kg (5 lb), squat and deadlift 5 kg (10 lb). A T1 that misses its total moves to 6x2, then 10x1, before the load is reset from a new five-rep max; a T2 moves from 3x10 to 3x8 to 3x6. A T3 goes up when its open set reaches 25 reps.
adapt: Written as a cycle, the stage ladder can be run: after a session that misses its total the coming sessions of that lift move to the next scheme (5x3 to 6x2 to 10x1; 3x10 to 3x8 to 3x6), and after the last stage the load is reset as the programme says. The four sessions fit a four-day week as written; on three days only three of them can be scheduled.
caveats: Well regarded. The failure ladder is the part people come to it for, and the part this app does not run.

name: Ivysaur 4-4-8
author: u/lvysaur (r/Fitness)
structure: Full body three times a week. Each main lift alternates a heavy day of 4x4 and a light day of 4x8 at about 90 % of the heavy load, the last set open-ended.
progression: Weekly steps: squat and deadlift 7.5 kg (15 lb), bench and row 5 kg (10 lb), overhead press 2.5 kg (5 lb). No formal deload; when last sets become maximal, narrow the rep range, and move on once several lifts stall.
adapt: Put the heavy and the light day of a lift in different routines. Written as a cycle, the light day is kept at about 90 % of the heavy load each week. The weekly steps are aggressive; smaller ones last longer.
caveats: Written to fix the low upper-body frequency of Starting Strength and StrongLifts. Many do not get through the full table at its steps.

name: Fierce 5
author: davisj3537 (bodybuilding.com forum)
structure: Two full-body sessions, alternated. A: squat 3x5, bench press 3x5, row 3x8, plus accessories. B: front squat 3x5, overhead press 3x5, Romanian deadlift 3x8, plus accessories.
progression: Main lifts add 2.5 kg (5 lb) upper body and 5 kg (10 lb) lower body when all sets are done; accessories work up a rep range before the load moves. Two sessions missed in a row on a lift take 10-15 % off.
adapt: The app trains one fixed week, so the A/B alternation becomes A-B-A every week. Accessories go on `double`.
caveats: A balanced exercise selection; often recommended as the novice programme that already has accessories.

name: Candito Linear Program
author: Jonnie Candito
structure: Upper/lower split over four days. Two heavy days hold squat and deadlift, and bench press, at 3x6; the other two days use variations chosen for control, power or size.
progression: Main lifts go up every week until they stall; a stall takes about 7 kg (15 lb) off that lift, and after three resets the lift moves up every second week.
adapt: Written as a cycle, main lifts go up once a week as the programme has it, a stall takes its fixed amount off, and a lift that has been reset three times moves every second week.
caveats: Only the outline was checked against the source; the details come from a summary.

name: Ice Cream Fitness 5x5
author: Jason Blaha
structure: StrongLifts-style 5x5 main lifts with curls, triceps work, shrugs and abdominal work added after them.
progression: Load goes up each session the sets are done; a miss takes about 10 % off.
adapt: The app trains one fixed week, so the A/B alternation becomes A-B-A every week.
caveats: Long sessions. Only its existence and outline are confirmed; the failure rules were not checked.

name: Barbell Medicine Beginner Prescription
author: Jordan Feigenbaum, Austin Baraki
structure: A three-phase introductory template that can be run again while it keeps working. Loads are chosen by effort (RPE), not from a table.
progression: Linear, steered by RPE. The rules were not checked.
adapt: The app does not choose loads from an effort rating. With progression off, the lifter picks each session's load and logs the effort.
caveats: Only its existence and three-phase shape are confirmed: days a week and the rules are unknown. RPE takes a newer lifter time to learn.
